results.title: Exa's Websets V2 Runs 4x Faster at Half the Cost for Web Research | AlphaSignal
results.content:
Exa has released Websets V2, an upgrade to its service for turning plain-English queries into structured datasets sourced from the web. Exa reports fourfold faster jobs, roughly half the previous cost, and 20% gains in both matching accuracy and recall. The company has also removed the monthly subscription for new users and opened API access to everyone. Existing integrations receive the performance improvements without code changes. [...] - Exa released Websets V2: 4x faster dataset building at roughly half the cost per match.
- Accuracy and recall are up 20%, and the gains apply automatically for all users with no code changes.
- The subscription is gone; pricing is now $0.10 per compute unit plus $5 per 1,000 searches.
- Every usage-plan user gets API access, billed from the same credits as Exa's Search API.
- On Exa's own benchmarks, V2 averaged $0.017 to $0.024 per verified match versus Claude Code, Gemini, and Parallel.
- Existing Starter and Pro users must opt in to the new pricing, and the switch can't be undone. [...] ## Lists that do not exist yet

Websets targets set discovery: finding many entities that satisfy several conditions at once. Conventional search engines rank pages, while chatbots often produce short lists with uneven sourcing. Websets assembles a structured result set from live web data and Exa's index of more than 1 billion people, 70 million companies, 1.2 billion products, and 500 million research papers. Each row includes sources and an explanation of how it matches the query.

results.title: Websets V2: 4x Faster, 2x Cheaper | Exa Blog
results.content:
Websets enables you to build massive datasets that answer complex questions. It searches the web and compares results against your specific requirements, creating custom datasets that don’t exist anywhere else.

With Websets, you can:

Every match becomes a row in your dataset. You can add new enrichment columns for new details you want to compare, such as links to a paper’s repo, a lab’s research focus, or a company’s recent initiatives. You can review the sources for each result and export each dataset for further analysis.

Explore example datasets coveringhealthcare companies mentioning AI in their 10-K filings, UK publications on AI in ecommerce, and 1,000 YC startups with batch and industry data. [...] > Exa Site Index
> 
> Fetch the Exa site index at:
> 
> Use this file to discover Exa products, pricing, evaluations, comparisons, use cases, agent interfaces, and technical documentation before exploring further.

Today we’re releasing Websets V2. You can now create massive datasets from the web 4x faster, and 2x cheaper.

Websets enables you to describe what you’re looking for in plain language, and build a list from live web data and Exa’s database of 1B+ people, 70M+ companies, 1.2B+ products, and 500M+ research papers. Each row includes sources and reasoning describing how each result matches your criteria. [...] The harder the search, the smaller the savings. The Vanguard search reviewed 454 candidates to find 100 matches and cost 98% less than before. The climate tech search reviewed over 6,000 candidates, but only 19 met every criterion, so it cost about the same per match as legacy pricing.

Across Websets V2 searches, the cost per match is about half the legacy Pro price on average. That is an average, not a guarantee. Usage-based pricing charges for the work a search does, even when it finds few or no matches, so a very hard search can cost more per match than it did before.

Read more on V2’s new pricing here.

Websets V2 is available today. Try a complex search and build your next dataset.
